title: PNB Targets Rs 6,000 Crore Quarterly Profit After Record September Quarter
excerpt: Net profit rose 12.8% to a record Rs 5,532 crore in Q2 FY27 as core operating profit grew about 29%, and CEO Ashok Chandra said the Rs 6,000 crore mark is a few quarters away.
body:
• Punjab National Bank posted a record net profit of Rs 5,532 crore in the September quarter of FY27, up 12.8% year on year, and CEO Ashok Chandra said Rs 6,000 crore in a quarter is reachable within a few quarters.
  • Core operating profit, excluding treasury gains and recoveries, rose about 29% year on year, even as treasury income fell to Rs 753 crore from Rs 1,769 crore a year earlier — a shortfall of about Rs 1,000 crore.
  • Asset quality improved: gross NPA fell to 2.55% from 2.78% in the June quarter, and net NPA to 0.25% from 0.28%.
  • For depositors and borrowers: PNB says it is in no hurry to raise deposit rates after the RBI's 25-basis-point repo hike, expects credit growth of 13-14% in FY27, and sees the hike lifting its net interest margin by 6-7 basis points in the December quarter.

Punjab National Bank is targeting quarterly net profit of Rs 6,000 crore over the next few quarters, Managing Director and CEO Ashok Chandra said after the state-owned lender posted its highest-ever quarterly profit of Rs 5,532 crore in the September quarter of FY27. The bank has maintained consistency in operating profit, net profit and other parameters over the past four quarters and expects the trend to continue, Chandra told PTI, according to the PTI interview published October 18.

"We are already at Rs 5,500 crore, and we are aiming to grow the operating profit, despite the treasury loss of around Rs 1,000 crore in this particular quarter compared to September 2025. Still, we have maintained the operating profit growth. I think just wait for a few quarters." — Ashok Chandra, MD and CEO, Punjab National Bank, to PTI

The September Quarter in Numbers

For the second quarter ended September 2026, PNB reported a 12.8% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 5,532 crore, supported by higher interest income and improving asset quality. Net interest income rose 10.8% to Rs 11,601 crore from Rs 10,468 crore in the year-ago quarter, and operating profit increased 4.2% to Rs 7,532 crore, according to the bank's results coverage. Global advances grew 14.7% year on year to Rs 13.41 lakh crore, while deposits rose 9.9% to Rs 17.77 lakh crore.

Asset quality improved on both measures. Gross NPAs fell to 2.55% from 2.78% in the preceding quarter and 3.45% a year ago, BusinessLine reported. Net NPAs fell to 0.25% from 0.28% in the June quarter. The bank also made a floating provision of Rs 125 crore, taking the cumulative total to Rs 2,560 crore, ahead of Expected Credit Loss guidelines effective April 1.

Core Profit Carried the Quarter

The headline operating profit growth understates the core business. Treasury income fell to Rs 753 crore from Rs 1,769 crore a year earlier. Core operating profit, excluding treasury gains and recoveries, grew about 29% year on year, after 32-34% growth in the previous quarter, Chandra said. Operating profit would have crossed Rs 8,500 crore if the treasury shortfall were added back, he said at the results briefing.

Lending growth was led by the retail, agriculture and MSME segments. Retail loans are growing at more than 16%, MSME advances by 19-20% and agriculture lending by more than 18%, Chandra told PTI. Corporate sanctions are rising 17-18%, while balance-sheet growth in corporate advances is 10-11%, partly because the bank is shedding low-yielding corporate loans. With festive demand, PNB expects a further 1-2% growth across those books in the third quarter.

Guidance: Faster Credit Growth, Better Margins

Chandra raised expected FY27 credit growth to 13-14%, against earlier guidance of 12-13%. The RBI's 25-basis-point repo hike could lift net interest margin by 6-7 basis points in the December quarter, he said. Global NIM improved to 2.58% in the September quarter from 2.50% in the preceding quarter; domestic NIM has touched 2.74%, and full-year NIM guidance remains 2.6-2.7%.

On deposits, the bank is holding rates. "I think we are not in a hurry to go in the market, raise the deposit rate, because as of now, we are quite comfortable," Chandra said, pointing to a credit-deposit ratio of around 75%, which leaves room to support lending even with deposit growth of 8-9%. The bank mobilised $2.7 billion through its foreign-currency non-resident deposit campaign, above its $2.5 billion target, to replace higher-cost deposits. It also plans to raise $1 billion under its Medium-Term Note programme when conditions are favourable, BusinessLine reported.

What to Watch

The target requires roughly 8.5% growth from Rs 5,532 crore, with core operating profit already growing near 29%. The variables are treasury income, which cost about Rs 1,000 crore year on year this quarter, and whether NIM reaches the guided 2.6-2.7% range. December quarter results will show whether the projected 6-7 basis point margin gain arrives on schedule.
